     3	module MPY-BUILTINS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-STR
     6	  imports MPY-SET
     7	  imports MPY-ITER
     8	  imports MPY-RANGE
     9	  imports MPY-INT
    10	  imports MPY-METHODS
    11	
    12	  // the builtins REGISTRY is core.k's builtinsScope (the -1 frame); names resolve by lookup
    13	
    14	  // Call routing + argument evaluation live in call.k, which also routes the fold
    15	  // builtins (sum/all/any/max/min) to the #_Acc folds below and everything else to
    16	  // applyBuiltin. This module owns applyBuiltin + the fold implementations.
    17	  syntax Val ::= applyBuiltin(String, Vals) [function]
    18	
    19	  // ==== len(obj) — O(1) per kind ============================================
    20	  syntax Int ::= seqLen(Val) [function]
    21	  rule applyBuiltin("len", OBJ:Val, .Vals) => seqLen(OBJ)
    22	  rule seqLen(list(VS:ValSeq))                  => vsLen(VS)
    23	  rule seqLen(tuple(VS:ValSeq))                 => vsLen(VS)
    24	  rule seqLen(str(IS:IntSeq))                   => isLen(IS)
    25	  rule seqLen(setV(DS:IntSeq))                  => isLen(DS)
    26	  rule seqLen(rangeObj(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int)) => rangeLen(LO, HI, ST)
    27	
    28	  // ==== list(seq) — materialize a list/tuple into a list (e.g. list(d.keys())) ==
    29	  // Minimal: the "copy a sequence" case (list of a list is itself; list of a tuple keeps order).
    30	  // list() of other iterables (str/range/set/zip) is added via the iterator fold when needed.
    31	  // (k-cell — list() constructs a NEW object)
    32	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), (list(VS:ValSeq),  .Vals)) => #alloc(list(VS)) ... </k>
    33	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), (tuple(VS:ValSeq), .Vals)) => #alloc(list(VS)) ... </k>
    34	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), .Vals)                     => #alloc(list(.ValSeq)) ... </k>
    35	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), (str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals))   => #alloc(list(charsOf(CS))) ... </k>
    36	  syntax ValSeq ::= charsOf(IntSeq) [function, total]
    37	  rule charsOf(.IntSeq)                => .ValSeq
    38	  rule charsOf(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => vCons(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), charsOf(R))
    39	
    40	  // ==== set(str) — distinct character codes =================================
    41	  rule applyBuiltin("set", str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals) => setV(dedupCodes(CS))
    42	
    43	  // ==== abs(int) ============================================================
    44	  rule applyBuiltin("abs", I:Int, .Vals) => absInt(I)
    45	
    46	  // ==== sum(iterable) — one #iterNext fold; intOf = int value of an int/bool ==
    47	  syntax KItem ::= #sumAcc(Iterable, Int) | #sumCont(Int)
    48	  rule <k> #sumAcc(IT:Iterable, ACC:Int) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #sumCont(ACC) ... </k>
    49	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #sumCont(ACC:Int) => ACC ... </k>
    50	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumCont(ACC:Int)
    51	        => #sumAcc(R, ACC +Int intOf(V)) ... </k>
    52	       requires isInt(V) orBool isBool(V)
    53	
    54	  syntax Int ::= intOf(Val) [function]
    55	  rule intOf(I:Int)  => I
    56	  rule intOf(B:Bool) => #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi
    57	
    58	  // ==== all / any (short-circuiting #iterNext folds) ========================
    59	  syntax KItem ::= #allAcc(Iterable) | "#allCont"
    60	  rule <k> #allAcc(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #allCont ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #allCont => true ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #allCont => #allAcc(R) ... </k>
    63	       requires truthy(V)
    64	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #allCont => false ... </k>
    65	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    66	
    67	  syntax KItem ::= #anyAcc(Iterable) | "#anyCont"
    68	  rule <k> #anyAcc(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #anyCont ... </k>
    69	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #anyCont => false ... </k>
    70	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #anyCont => true ... </k>
    71	       requires truthy(V)
    72	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #anyCont => #anyAcc(R) ... </k>
    73	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    74	
    75	  // ==== max / min over an iterable (#iterNext folds; first element seeds) ====
    76	  syntax KItem ::= #maxAcc0(Iterable) | "#maxCont0" | #maxAcc(Iterable, Int) | #maxCont(Int)
    77	  rule <k> #maxAcc0(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxCont0 ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont0 => #maxAcc(R, {V}:>Int) ... </k>
    79	       requires isInt(V)
    80	  rule <k> #maxAcc(IT:Iterable, M:Int) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxCont(M) ... </k>
    81	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #maxCont(M:Int) => M ... </k>
    82	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont(M:Int)
    83	        => #maxAcc(R, maxInt(M, {V}:>Int)) ... </k>
    84	       requires isInt(V)
    85	
    86	  syntax KItem ::= #minAcc0(Iterable) | "#minCont0" | #minAcc(Iterable, Int) | #minCont(Int)
    87	  rule <k> #minAcc0(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minCont0 ... </k>
    88	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont0 => #minAcc(R, {V}:>Int) ... </k>
    89	       requires isInt(V)
    90	  rule <k> #minAcc(IT:Iterable, M:Int) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minCont(M) ... </k>
    91	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #minCont(M:Int) => M ... </k>
    92	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont(M:Int)
    93	        => #minAcc(R, minInt(M, {V}:>Int)) ... </k>
    94	       requires isInt(V)
    95	
    96	  // ==== variadic max / min (a Vals fold) ====================================
    97	  syntax Int ::= maxVals(Int, Vals) [function]
    98	  rule applyBuiltin("max", I:Int, REST:Vals) => maxVals(I, REST)
    99	  rule maxVals(M:Int, .Vals)           => M
   100	  rule maxVals(M:Int, (I:Int, R:Vals)) => maxVals(maxInt(M, I), R)
   101	
   102	  syntax Int ::= minVals(Int, Vals) [function]
   103	  rule applyBuiltin("min", I:Int, REST:Vals) => minVals(I, REST)
   104	  rule minVals(M:Int, .Vals)           => M
   105	  rule minVals(M:Int, (I:Int, R:Vals)) => minVals(minInt(M, I), R)
   106	
   107	  // ==== bin(n) — "0b" + binary digit codes (promoted from 103's defined fold) ==
   108	  rule applyBuiltin("bin", N:Int, .Vals) => str(iCons(48, iCons(98, binCodes(N))))
   109	       requires N >=Int 0
   110	  // negative operand: the '-' sign prefixes the magnitude's digits
   111	  rule applyBuiltin("bin", N:Int, .Vals)
   112	    => str(iCons(45, iCons(48, iCons(98, binCodes(0 -Int N)))))
   113	       requires N <Int 0
   114	  syntax IntSeq ::= binCodes(Int) [function, total]
   115	  rule binCodes(0) => iCons(48, .IntSeq)
   116	  rule binCodes(N:Int) => binAcc(N, .IntSeq) requires N >Int 0
   117	  syntax IntSeq ::= binAcc(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
   118	  rule binAcc(0, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
   119	  rule binAcc(N:Int, ACC:IntSeq)
   120	    => binAcc((N -Int pyMod(N, 2)) /Int 2, iCons(48 +Int pyMod(N, 2), ACC))
   121	       requires N >Int 0
   122	
   123	  // ==== enumerate(xs) — pairs (i, v); materialized eagerly over a list =========
   124	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("enumerate")), (list(VS:ValSeq), .Vals))
   125	        => #alloc(list(enumVS(VS, 0))) ... </k>
   126	  syntax ValSeq ::= enumVS(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]
   127	  rule enumVS(.ValSeq, _:Int) => .ValSeq
   128	  rule enumVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), I:Int)

    29	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (ref(H:Int), .Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    30	       [priority(40)]
    31	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       requires truthy(V)
    34	       [priority(40)]
    35	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    36	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    37	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    38	       [priority(40)]
    39	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       requires truthy(V)
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/list.k — MPY-LIST
     2	
     3	module MPY-LIST
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     7	
     8	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
    13	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
    14	  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
    15	  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>
    16	
    17	  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    19	  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
    20	  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))
    21	
    22	  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
    23	  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
    24	  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>
    25	       [priority(45)]
    26	
    27	  rule applyCmp("==", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    29	
    30	  // ==== deep equality when elements are heap objects (list-of-lists) ========
    31	  // Python == is structural at every depth. Fires ONLY when a ref is present
    32	  // (the guard decides on concrete seqs); the plain ==K path above is unchanged.
    33	  syntax Bool ::= hasRefVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    34	  rule hasRefVS(.ValSeq)                => false
    35	  rule hasRefVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => isRefV(V) orBool hasRefVS(R)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= deepEqVS(ValSeq, ValSeq, Map) [function]
    38	                | deepEqV(Val, Val, Map)        [function]
    39	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:Map)                   => true
    40	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), _:Map)    => false
    41	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq, _:Map)    => false
    42	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq), HP:Map)
    43	    => deepEqV(A, B, HP) andBool deepEqVS(As, Bs, HP)
    44	
    45	  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
    46	       requires H in_keys(HP)
    47	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
    48	       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
    49	  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
    50	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]
    51	
    52	  // ==== mutator: xs.append(v) — an in-place heap write ======================
    53	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "append")), (V:Val, .Vals)) => noneV ... </k>
    54	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq))) ... </heap>
    55	       [priority(40)]
    56	
    57	  // ==== `x in list` — a <k>-cell fold over #iterNext ========================
    58	  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
    59	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
    60	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #memberAcc(V:Val, IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #memberCont(V) ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #memberCont(_V:Val) => false ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    64	       requires E ==K V
    65	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    66	       requires notBool (E ==K V)
    67	  rule <k> B:Bool ~> #notB => notBool B ... </k>
    68	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/set.k — MPY-SET
     2	
     3	module MPY-SET
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // a set value, carried as its distinct codes in first-seen order (order is irrelevant
     7	  // to membership/cardinality — the two observations sets support here).
     8	  syntax Val ::= setV(IntSeq)
     9	
    10	  // membership of a code in the accumulated distinct-code sequence
    11	  syntax Bool ::= codeIn(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
    12	  rule codeIn(_:Int, .IntSeq)                => false
    13	  rule codeIn(C:Int, iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq)) => C ==Int H orBool codeIn(C, T)
    14	
    15	  // the distinct codes of CS (insert-if-absent fold, first-seen order)
    16	  syntax IntSeq ::= dedupCodes(IntSeq)         [function, total]
    17	                  | dedupFrom(IntSeq, IntSeq)  [function, total]
    18	  rule dedupCodes(CS:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(CS, .IntSeq)
    19	  rule dedupFrom(.IntSeq, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
    20	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, ACC)
    21	       requires codeIn(C, ACC)
    22	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, snocCode(ACC, C))
    23	       requires notBool codeIn(C, ACC)
    24	
    25	  syntax IntSeq ::= snocCode(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
    26	  rule snocCode(.IntSeq, C:Int)                => iCons(C, .IntSeq)
    27	  rule snocCode(iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq), C:Int) => iCons(H, snocCode(T, C))
    28	
    29	  // ==== set equality: two sets are equal iff mutually subsuming ==============
    30	  // subsetCodes(A, B) — every code of A occurs in B (duplicates in A are harmless).
    31	  syntax Bool ::= subsetCodes(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    32	  rule subsetCodes(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)                => true
    33	  rule subsetCodes(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), B:IntSeq) => codeIn(C, B) andBool subsetCodes(S, B)
    34	
    35	  syntax Bool ::= sameSet(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    36	  rule sameSet(A:IntSeq, B:IntSeq) => subsetCodes(A, B) andBool subsetCodes(B, A)
    37	
    38	  // set == set  (the only comparison sets support here)
    39	  rule applyCmp("==", setV(A:IntSeq), setV(B:IntSeq)) => sameSet(A, B)
    40	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/assert.k — MPY-ASSERT
     2	
     3	module MPY-ASSERT
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  rule <k> Assert(V:Val) => .K ... </k>
     7	       requires truthy(V)
     8	  rule <k> Assert(V:Val) ~> _ => .K </k>
     9	       <exc> NoExc => AssertionError </exc>
    10	       <exit-code> _ => 1 </exit-code>
    11	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    12	
    13	  rule <k> Assert(ref(H:Int)) => Assert(V) ... </k>
    14	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    15	       [priority(40)]
    16	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/comprehension.k — MPY-COMPREHENSION
     2	
     3	module MPY-COMPREHENSION
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     6	  imports MPY-LIST
     7	  imports MPY-CONTROLS
     8	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
     9	
    10	  // A comprehension is pure syntactic sugar
    11	  rule ListComp(ELT:Expr, Gs:CompFors) => Call(closureExpr(.ParamNames, compBody(Gs, ELT)), .Exprs)
    12	  rule GenExp(ELT:Expr, Gs:CompFors)   => Call(closureExpr(.ParamNames, compBody(Gs, ELT)), .Exprs)
    13	
    14	  syntax Stmts ::= compBody(CompFors, Expr) [macro]
    15	  rule compBody(Gs:CompFors, ELT:Expr)
    16	    => Assign(Name("$acc"), ListExpr(.Exprs)) compNest(Gs, ELT) Return(Name("$acc"))
    17	
    18	  syntax Stmt ::= compNest(CompFors, Expr) [macro-rec]
    19	  rule compNest(.CompFors, ELT:Expr)
    20	    => Assign(Name("$acc"), BinOp("+", Name("$acc"), ListExpr(ELT)))
    21	  rule compNest((CompFor(T:Expr, ITER:Expr, Fs:Exprs) GRest:CompFors), ELT:Expr)
    22	    => For(T, ITER, If(compGuard(Fs), compNest(GRest, ELT), .Stmts))
    23	
    24	  syntax Expr ::= compGuard(Exprs) [macro]
    25	  rule compGuard(.Exprs)             => Bool(true)
    26	  rule compGuard((F:Expr, Fs:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (F, Fs))
    27	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/dict.k — MPY-DICT
     2	//
     3	// Minimal dict support. A dict value is `dictV(KS, VS)`: PARALLEL insertion-ordered key/value
     4	// ValSeqs (Python dict order; keys distinct; re-inserting a key updates its value in place, keeping
     5	// the original position). Concrete for krun (the ordered build + `.keys()` are the real ops); a proof
     6	// over a SYMBOLIC dict passes `dictV(KS, WS)` with a symbolic key sequence KS and reads
     7	// `d.keys() = list(KS)`, then keeps each key opaque problem-locally.
     8	//
     9	// Only the pieces needed so far: a dict VALUE (so `{}` inside a mixed list evaluates and
    10	// `isinstance(x, int)` rejects it), the `{k: v, ...}` literal, and `.keys()`. More dict ops (subscript
    11	// / `.get()` / `.values()` / dict `==`) are added as dict problems need them — kept minimal + additive.
    12	
    13	module MPY-DICT
    14	  imports MPY-CORE
    15	  imports MPY-ITER
    16	  imports MPY-METHODS
    17	  imports MPY-LIST
    18	
    19	  // dict as PARALLEL ordered key/value ValSeqs (same length; keys distinct).
    20	  syntax Val ::= dictV(ValSeq, ValSeq)
    21	
    22	  // ==== DictExpr: {k: v, ...} literal. Eval each key then value, left to right, insert-with-dedup.
    23	  syntax KItem ::= #dictAcc(Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    24	                 | #dictKey(Expr, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    25	                 | #dictVal(Val, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    26	  rule <k> DictExpr(ES:Entries) => #dictAcc(ES, .ValSeq, .ValSeq) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #dictAcc(.Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq) => dictV(KS, VS) ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #dictAcc((Entry(K:Expr, V:Expr), REST:Entries), KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    29	        => K ~> #dictKey(V, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dictKey(V:Expr, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    31	        => V ~> #dictVal(KV, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    32	  rule <k> VV:Val ~> #dictVal(KV:Val, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    33	        => #dictAcc(REST, dPutK(KS, KV), dPutV(KS, VS, KV, VV)) ... </k>
    34	
    35	  // insert-with-dedup helpers (concrete Val key equality via ==K). [total] so buildFold over a dict is
    36	  // total (its #Ceil is #Top) — needed when a symbolic proof carries a built dict as a config value.
    37	  syntax Bool ::= dHasKey(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    38	  rule dHasKey(.ValSeq, _:Val)                => false
    39	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => true          requires A ==K K
    40	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), K:Val) => dHasKey(R, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
    41	
    42	  // dPutK: KS unchanged if K already present, else append K (keep-first-position).
    43	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutK(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    44	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => KS                                  requires dHasKey(KS, K)
    45	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => valSeqConcat(KS, vCons(K, .ValSeq)) requires notBool dHasKey(KS, K)
    46	
    47	  // dPutV: parallel to KS — set the value at K's position if present, else append V at the end. The
    48	  // [owise] catch-all covers the degenerate mismatched-length case (never reached for a well-formed dict).
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutV(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val, Val) [function, total]
    50	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)  => vCons(V, VR)
    51	       requires A ==K K
    52	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(B, dPutV(KR, VR, K, V))
    53	       requires notBool (A ==K K)
    54	  rule dPutV(_KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq, _K:Val, V:Val) => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq)) [owise]
    55	
    56	  // ==== dict methods ========================================================
    57	  // d.keys() -> a FRESH list object of the ordered keys (k-cell: it allocates).
    58	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(dictV(KS:ValSeq, _:ValSeq), "keys")), .Vals)
    59	        => #alloc(list(KS)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	
    62	  // ==== dict subscript READ: d[k] (assoc lookup; KeyError is out of subset) ==
    63	  rule applyIndexD(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KS, VS, K)
    64	  syntax Val ::= applyIndexD(Val, Val) [function]
    65	  rule <k> Subscript(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => applyIndexD(dictV(KS, VS), K) ... </k>
    66	       [priority(45)]
    67	
    68	  // ==== dict subscript-assign: d[k] = v (insert/update in place) =============
    69	  // Only for a LOCAL dict variable X (the current scope holds it). Reuses dPutK/dPutV.
    70	  syntax Val ::= dictSet(Val, Val, Val) [function]
    71	  rule dictSet(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => dictV(dPutK(KS, K), dPutV(KS, VS, K, V))
    72	
    73	  // RHS evaluates first (Assign strictness), then the key. Dispatch on the scope
    74	  // value: a bare dict updates in the scope (dicts stay values); a ref (a heap
    75	  // list — or a heap dict later) writes the heap in place.
    76	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetK(String, Val)
    77	  rule <k> Assign(Subscript(Name(X:String), K:Expr), VV:Val) => K ~> #dsetK(X, VV) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    79	       <env> L:Int </env>
    80	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- dictSet({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ], _) ... </scopes>
    81	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool notBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    82	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => #dsetV({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ... </k>
    83	       <env> L:Int </env>
    84	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    85	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    86	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetV(Val, Val, Val)
    87	  rule <k> #dsetV(ref(H:Int), I:Int, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    88	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => setVSAt(VS, normIdxD(I, vsLen(VS)), VV)) ... </heap>
    89	  // negative-index normalization local to the write (subscript.k's is not imported here)
    90	  syntax Int ::= normIdxD(Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    92	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    93	
    94	  // ==== dict == (order-insensitive: same size + same key->value pairs) =======
    95	  rule applyCmp("==", dictV(KS1:ValSeq, VS1:ValSeq), dictV(KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq))
    96	    => (vsLen(KS1) ==Int vsLen(KS2)) andBool dSubset(KS1, VS1, KS2, VS2)
    97	  syntax Bool ::= dSubset(ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    98	  rule dSubset(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:ValSeq, _:ValSeq) => true
    99	  rule dSubset(vCons(K:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(V:Val, VR:ValSeq), KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq)
   100	    => dHasKey(KS2, K) andBool (dGet(KS2, VS2, K) ==K V) andBool dSubset(KR, VR, KS2, VS2)
   101	  syntax Val ::= dGet(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val) [function]
   102	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => B                requires A ==K K
   103	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KR, VR, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
   104	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/sort.k — MPY-SORT
     2	// Trusted sorted(): sorted(list) as an opaque ascending permutation `sortVS` — opaque symbolic
     3	// for kprove (a trusted primitive, correctness/ordering proved in Lean / notes/sort-probe),
     4	// and a concrete insertion sort for krun. Wrappers verify the logic AROUND the sort (index /
     5	// slice / filter / dedup); indexing an opaque sortVS(VS) carries through as an opaque term, so
     6	// no ordering lemma is needed in K — the trust (sortVS = real sorted) is discharged by each
     7	// problem's differential test. Only int lists (compared by projectIntTotal); keyed / string
     8	// sorts are separate. Fires only via the "sorted" builtin, so inert for non-sorting programs.
     9	
    10	module MPY-SORT
    11	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    12	  imports MPY-SUBSCRIPT
    13	
    14	  // sortVS(VS): the ascending sort of the Val list VS. Opaque for symbolic VS (no-evaluators);
    15	  // concrete insertion sort for krun.
    16	  // Concrete sort matches Int-sorted elements directly (an int Val IS an Int); projectIntTotal
    17	  // (lemmas-only) is not available in the semantics. Int and str lists.
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= sortVS(ValSeq) [function, total, symbol(sortVS), no-evaluators]
    19	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVS(Int, ValSeq) [function]
    20	  rule sortVS(.ValSeq)                => .ValSeq          [concrete]
    21	  rule sortVS(vCons(X:Int, R:ValSeq)) => insVS(X, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    22	  rule insVS(X:Int, .ValSeq)                => vCons(X, .ValSeq) [concrete]
    23	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(X, vCons(Y, R)) requires X <=Int Y [concrete]
    24	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(Y, insVS(X, R)) requires X  >Int Y [concrete]
    25	  // str elements insert by the shared lexicographic strLt (methods.k)
    26	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVSs(IntSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    27	  rule sortVS(vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => insVSs(CS, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    28	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, .ValSeq) => vCons(str(A), .ValSeq) [concrete]
    29	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(A), vCons(str(B), R))
    30	       requires strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B [concrete]
    31	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(B), insVSs(A, R))
    32	       requires notBool (strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B) [concrete]
    33	
    34	  // sorted(list) constructs a NEW object: k-cell pre-dispatch (beats the [owise]
    35	  // applyBuiltin routing in call.k) so the result allocates.
    36	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), .Vals))
    37	        => #alloc(list(sortVS(VS))) ... </k>
    38	
    39	  // mutator: xs.sort() — the in-place heap write over the same trusted sortVS
    40	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "sort")), .Vals) => noneV ... </k>
    41	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => sortVS(VS)) ... </heap>
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  // ==== keyed / reversed sorted() (WP2) =====================================
    45	  // sortKeyVS(VS, KV): the stable ascending sort of VS by the key value KV
    46	  // (a closure/builtin/type — anything callable). OPAQUE here; the concrete
    47	  // leg (MPY-CONCRETE, llvm only) computes keys by REAL calls and stable-
    48	  // inserts, at priority(40) over these.
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= sortKeyVS(ValSeq, Val) [function, total, symbol(sortKeyVS), no-evaluators]
    50	
    51	  syntax ValSeq ::= revVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    52	                  | revVSAcc(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    53	  rule revVS(S:ValSeq) => revVSAcc(S, .ValSeq)
    54	  rule revVSAcc(.ValSeq, A:ValSeq) => A
    55	  rule revVSAcc(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), A:ValSeq) => revVSAcc(R, vCons(V, A))
    56	
    57	  syntax ValSeq ::= condRev(ValSeq, Bool) [function, total]
    58	  rule condRev(S:ValSeq, false) => S
    59	  rule condRev(S:ValSeq, true)  => revVS(S)

   237	  // ---- min / max over a FLOAT list — FLOAT branch of the shared #minCont0/#maxCont0 folds (which
   238	  // seed/step with `requires isInt(V)`, so they are STUCK on floats). These add the `requires
   239	  // isFloat(V)` seed + a Float-accumulator fold via K's minFloat/maxFloat — concrete for krun. A proof
   240	  // over a SYMBOLIC float list intercepts min/max problem-locally to an opaque minVF/maxVF (at
   241	  // #applyK, priority 40, in its verification.k) BEFORE #minAcc0, so this fold is krun-only. Additive:
   242	  // the isFloat guard is disjoint from the existing isInt one.
   243	  syntax KItem ::= #maxAccF(Iterable, Float) | #maxContF(Float)
   244	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont0 => #maxAccF(R, {V}:>Float) ... </k> requires isFloat(V)
   245	  rule <k> #maxAccF(IT:Iterable, M:Float) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxContF(M) ... </k>
   246	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #maxContF(M:Float) => M ... </k>
   247	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxContF(M:Float) => #maxAccF(R, maxFloat(M, {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
   248	       requires isFloat(V)
   249	
   250	  syntax KItem ::= #minAccF(Iterable, Float) | #minContF(Float)
   251	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont0 => #minAccF(R, {V}:>Float) ... </k> requires isFloat(V)
   252	  rule <k> #minAccF(IT:Iterable, M:Float) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minContF(M) ... </k>
   253	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #minContF(M:Float) => M ... </k>
   254	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minContF(M:Float) => #minAccF(R, minFloat(M, {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
   255	       requires isFloat(V)
   256	
   257	  // ---- sum over a float list (krun; mirrors the min/max float paths). The Int-only shared
   258	  // #sumCont sticks on a Float yield; switch to a Float-headed fold via addF (concrete twin).
   259	  // The switch guard carries the SYNTACTIC negation of the Int rule's guard so a symbolic proof
   260	  // with isInt(V) in its path condition refutes this branch without sort reasoning.
   261	  syntax KItem ::= #sumAccF(Iterable, Float) | #sumContF(Float)
   262	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumCont(ACC:Int)
   263	        => #sumAccF(R, addF(intToF(ACC), {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
   264	       requires isFloat(V) andBool notBool (isInt(V) orBool isBool(V))
   265	  rule <k> #sumAccF(IT:Iterable, ACC:Float) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #sumContF(ACC) ... </k>
   266	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #sumContF(ACC:Float) => ACC ... </k>
   267	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumContF(ACC:Float)
   268	        => #sumAccF(R, addF(ACC, {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
   269	       requires isFloat(V)
   270	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumContF(ACC:Float)
   271	        => #sumAccF(R, addF(ACC, intToF(intOf(V)))) ... </k>
   272	       requires isInt(V) orBool isBool(V)
   273	endmodule

    24	  // S.join(list-of-str): fold with separator codes (receiver + arg deref'd by

    28	  rule joinCodes(_:IntSeq, .ValSeq) => .IntSeq
    29	  rule joinCodes(_:IntSeq, vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), .ValSeq)) => CS
    30	  rule joinCodes(SEP:IntSeq, vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)))

    33	  // S.count(sub): non-overlapping window scan (Python str.count)
    34	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "count", str(PC:IntSeq), .Vals) => cntSub(CS, PC)
    35	  syntax Int ::= cntSub(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function]
    36	  rule cntSub(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq) => 0
    37	  rule cntSub(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), PC:IntSeq) => 1 +Int cntSub(dropIS(iCons(C, R), isLen(PC)), PC)
    38	       requires strPrefix(PC, iCons(C, R)) andBool isLen(PC) >Int 0
    39	  rule cntSub(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), PC:IntSeq) => cntSub(R, PC)
    40	       requires notBool strPrefix(PC, iCons(C, R)) orBool isLen(PC) <=Int 0
    41	  syntax IntSeq ::= dropIS(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
    42	  rule dropIS(S:IntSeq, N:Int) => S requires N <=Int 0
    43	  rule dropIS(.IntSeq, _:Int) => .IntSeq [owise]
    44	  rule dropIS(iCons(_:Int, R:IntSeq), N:Int) => dropIS(R, N -Int 1) requires N >Int 0
    45	
    46	  // S.strip(): trim whitespace runs from both ends
    47	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "strip", .Vals) => str(revIS(trimWS(revIS(trimWS(CS)))))
    48	  syntax IntSeq ::= trimWS(IntSeq) [function, total]
    49	  rule trimWS(.IntSeq) => .IntSeq
    50	  rule trimWS(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => trimWS(R) requires isWSC(C)
    51	  rule trimWS(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => iCons(C, R) requires notBool isWSC(C)
    52	  syntax IntSeq ::= revIS(IntSeq) [function, total] | revISAcc(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    53	  rule revIS(S:IntSeq) => revISAcc(S, .IntSeq)
    54	  rule revISAcc(.IntSeq, A:IntSeq) => A
    55	  rule revISAcc(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:IntSeq) => revISAcc(R, iCons(C, A))
    56	
    57	  // S.encode('ascii'): identity on the code-sequence model (bytes == codes)
    58	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "encode", str(_:IntSeq), .Vals) => str(CS)
    59	
    60	  // ==== prefix ===============================================================
    61	  rule applyMethod(str(XC:IntSeq), "startswith", str(PC:IntSeq), .Vals) => startsWith(PC, XC)
    62	
    63	  // ==== list.count(v) — number of occurrences of v in the list (concrete for krun) ==========
    64	  rule applyMethod(list(VS:ValSeq), "count", V:Val, .Vals) => cntOccVS(VS, V)
    65	  syntax Int ::= cntOccVS(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    66	  rule cntOccVS(.ValSeq, _:Val)                => 0
    67	  rule cntOccVS(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), V:Val) => 1 +Int cntOccVS(R, V) requires A ==K V
    68	  rule cntOccVS(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), V:Val) => cntOccVS(R, V)        requires notBool (A ==K V)
    69	
    70	  // ==== split (no-arg: on whitespace runs, dropping empty tokens) + replace (single char) ==========
    71	  // Concrete string ops for krun. A proof over a symbolic string intercepts the split problem-locally.
    72	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(str(CS:IntSeq), "split")), .Vals)
    73	        => #alloc(list(splitWS(CS, .IntSeq, .ValSeq))) ... </k>
    74	       [priority(40)]
    75	  syntax ValSeq ::= splitWS(IntSeq, IntSeq, ValSeq) [function]  // remaining, current token, result
    76	  rule splitWS(.IntSeq, CUR:IntSeq, ACC:ValSeq) => flushTok(ACC, CUR)
    77	  rule splitWS(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), CUR:IntSeq, ACC:ValSeq) => splitWS(R, .IntSeq, flushTok(ACC, CUR))
    78	       requires isWSC(C)
    79	  rule splitWS(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), CUR:IntSeq, ACC:ValSeq) => splitWS(R, seqConcat(CUR, iCons(C, .IntSeq)), ACC)
    80	       requires notBool isWSC(C)
    81	  // flush the current token to the result list iff non-empty.
    82	  syntax ValSeq ::= flushTok(ValSeq, IntSeq) [function]
    83	  rule flushTok(ACC:ValSeq, .IntSeq)            => ACC
    84	  rule flushTok(ACC:ValSeq, iCons(C:Int, T:IntSeq)) => valSeqConcat(ACC, vCons(str(iCons(C, T)), .ValSeq))
    85	  syntax Bool ::= isWSC(Int) [function, total]
    86	  rule isWSC(C:Int) => C ==Int 32 orBool C ==Int 9 orBool C ==Int 10 orBool C ==Int 13
    87	
    88	  // split(sep='x') keyword form delegates to the positional k-cell rule
    89	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(str(CS:IntSeq), "split")), (kwV("sep", str(S:IntSeq)), .Vals))
    90	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(str(CS), "split")), (str(S), .Vals)) ... </k>
    91	       [priority(39)]
    92	
    93	  // str.split(sep) — single-char separator, KEEPING empty parts (Python's sep-split; len == #sep + 1).
    94	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(str(CS:IntSeq), "split")), (str(iCons(SEP:Int, .IntSeq)), .Vals))
    95	        => #alloc(list(splitSep(CS, SEP, .IntSeq))) ... </k>
    96	       [priority(40)]
    97	  syntax ValSeq ::= splitSep(IntSeq, Int, IntSeq) [function]  // remaining, sep code, current token
    98	  rule splitSep(.IntSeq, _SEP:Int, CUR:IntSeq)              => vCons(str(CUR), .ValSeq)
    99	  rule splitSep(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), SEP:Int, CUR:IntSeq) => vCons(str(CUR), splitSep(R, SEP, .IntSeq))
   100	       requires C ==Int SEP
   101	  rule splitSep(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), SEP:Int, CUR:IntSeq) => splitSep(R, SEP, seqConcat(CUR, iCons(C, .IntSeq)))
   102	       requires notBool (C ==Int SEP)
   103	
   104	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "replace", str(iCons(A:Int, .IntSeq)), str(iCons(B:Int, .IntSeq)), .Vals)
   105	    => str(replaceC(CS, A, B))
   106	  syntax IntSeq ::= replaceC(IntSeq, Int, Int) [function, total]
   107	  rule replaceC(.IntSeq, _:Int, _:Int)             => .IntSeq
   108	  rule replaceC(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int, B:Int) => iCons(B, replaceC(R, A, B)) requires C ==Int A
   109	  rule replaceC(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int, B:Int) => iCons(C, replaceC(R, A, B)) requires notBool (C ==Int A)
   110	
   111	  // ==== char helpers =========================================================
   112	  syntax Bool ::= isUpperC(Int) [function, total]
   113	  rule isUpperC(C:Int) => C >=Int 65 andBool C <=Int 90
   114	
   115	  syntax Bool ::= isLowerC(Int) [function, total]
   116	  rule isLowerC(C:Int) => C >=Int 97 andBool C <=Int 122
   117	
   118	  syntax Bool ::= isAlphaC(Int) [function, total]
   119	  rule isAlphaC(C:Int) => isUpperC(C) orBool isLowerC(C)
   120	
   121	  syntax Bool ::= isDigitC(Int) [function, total]
   122	  rule isDigitC(C:Int) => C >=Int 48 andBool C <=Int 57
   123	
   124	  syntax Bool ::= hasUpper(IntSeq) [function, total]
   125	  rule hasUpper(.IntSeq) => false
   126	  rule hasUpper(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => isUpperC(C) orBool hasUpper(S)
   127	
   128	  syntax Bool ::= hasLower(IntSeq) [function, total]
   129	  rule hasLower(.IntSeq) => false
   130	  rule hasLower(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => isLowerC(C) orBool hasLower(S)

   132	  syntax Bool ::= allAlpha(IntSeq) [function, total]

   134	  rule allAlpha(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => isAlphaC(C) andBool allAlpha(S)

   136	  syntax Bool ::= allDigit(IntSeq) [function, total]

   138	  rule allDigit(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => isDigitC(C) andBool allDigit(S)

   140	  syntax Int ::= lowerC(Int) [function, total]
   141	
   142	  rule lowerC(C:Int) => C +Int 32 requires isUpperC(C)
   143	  rule lowerC(C:Int) => C         [owise]
   144	
   145	  syntax Int ::= upperC(Int) [function, total]
   146	  rule upperC(C:Int) => C -Int 32 requires isLowerC(C)
   147	  rule upperC(C:Int) => C         [owise]
   148	
   149	  syntax Int ::= swapC(Int) [function, total]
   150	  rule swapC(C:Int) => C +Int 32 requires isUpperC(C)
   151	  rule swapC(C:Int) => C -Int 32 requires isLowerC(C)
   152	  rule swapC(C:Int) => C         [owise]

   156	  rule mapLower(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => iCons(lowerC(C), mapLower(S))

     2	
     3	module MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // ==== positional access + negative-index normalization (used only here) ===
     7	  // valSeqAt is [total]: in-bounds vCons access reduces as usual; on an OPAQUE sequence (e.g.
     8	  // a trusted sort's sortVS(VS)) or OOB it stays an abstract total value — so indexing the
     9	  // opaque sorted list is DEFINED (no undischarged #Ceil), matching the old semantics' total
    10	  // atK. K trusts the [total] annotation; valid programs index in-bounds.
    11	  syntax Val ::= valSeqAt(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]
    12	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(V:Val, _:ValSeq), 0)     => V
    13	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    14	       requires I >Int 0
    15	
    16	  syntax Int ::= intSeqAt(IntSeq, Int) [function]
    17	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(C:Int, _:IntSeq), 0)     => C
    18	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq), I:Int) => intSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    19	       requires I >Int 0
    20	
    21	  syntax Int ::= normIdx(Int, Int) [function, total]
    22	  rule normIdx(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    23	  rule normIdx(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    24	
    25	  // ==== Subscript: indexing obj[i] (list / tuple / str) =====================
    26	  // contexts (not strict attrs): the Index slot's Slice alternative must never heat
    27	  context Subscript(HOLE, _)
    28	  context Subscript(_:Val, HOLE:Expr)
    29	
    30	  // heap-object deref (covers both the index and slice forms via the Index slot)
    31	  rule <k> Subscript(ref(H:Int), IX:Index) => Subscript(V, IX) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	
    35	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, I:Int) => applyIndex(OBJ, I) ... </k>
    36	
    37	  syntax Val ::= applyIndex(Val, Int) [function]
    38	  rule applyIndex(list(VS:ValSeq),  I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    39	  rule applyIndex(tuple(VS:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    40	  rule applyIndex(str(IS:IntSeq),   I:Int)
    41	    => str(iCons(intSeqAt(IS, normIdx(I, isLen(IS))), .IntSeq))
    42	
    43	  // ==== Slice: obj[lo:hi:step] (list / str) — CPython slice.indices ==========
    44	  syntax KItem ::= #evalB(Bound) | "#toSome"
    45	                 | #slLo(Val, Bound, Bound)
    46	                 | #slHi(Val, OptInt, Bound)
    47	                 | #slStep(Val, OptInt, OptInt)
    48	
    49	  syntax OptInt ::= "noB" | someB(Int)
    50	  rule <k> #evalB(NoBound)  => noB ... </k>
    51	  rule <k> #evalB(E:Expr)   => E ~> #toSome ... </k>
    52	  rule <k> I:Int ~> #toSome => someB(I) ... </k>
    53	
    54	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, Slice(LO:Bound, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)) => #evalB(LO) ~> #slLo(OBJ, HI, ST) ... </k>
    55	  rule <k> LO:OptInt ~> #slLo(OBJ:Val, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)   => #evalB(HI) ~> #slHi(OBJ, LO, ST) ... </k>
    56	  rule <k> HI:OptInt ~> #slHi(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, ST:Bound)  => #evalB(ST) ~> #slStep(OBJ, LO, HI) ... </k>
    57	  // a list slice constructs a NEW object; a str slice stays a value
    58	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt)
    59	        => #alloc(doSlice(list(VS), LO, HI, ST)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(45)]
    61	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt) => doSlice(OBJ, LO, HI, ST) ... </k>
    62	
    63	  syntax Val ::= doSlice(Val, OptInt, OptInt, OptInt) [function]
    64	  rule doSlice(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    65	    => list(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    66	  rule doSlice(tuple(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    67	    => tuple(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    68	  rule doSlice(str(IS:IntSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    69	    => str(buildIS(IS, slStart(LO, ST, isLen(IS)), slStop(HI, ST, isLen(IS)), slStep(ST)))
    70	
    71	  // ==== slice.indices: step / start / stop / clamp ==========================
    72	  syntax Int ::= slStep(OptInt) [function, total]
    73	  rule slStep(noB)          => 1
    74	  rule slStep(someB(S:Int)) => S
    75	
    76	  syntax Int ::= slStart(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    77	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => 0
    78	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    79	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN -Int 1
    80	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    81	  rule slStart(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    82	
    83	  syntax Int ::= slStop(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    84	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN
    85	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    86	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => -1
    87	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    88	  rule slStop(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    89	
    90	  syntax Int ::= slAdjust(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampLo(I +Int LEN, STEP)
    92	       requires I  <Int 0
    93	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampHi(I, LEN, STEP)
    94	       requires I >=Int 0
    95	
    96	  syntax Int ::= clampLo(Int, Int) [function, total]
    97	  rule clampLo(J:Int, _STEP:Int) => J
    98	       requires J >=Int 0
    99	  rule clampLo(J:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then -1 #else 0 #fi
   100	       requires J <Int 0
   101	
   102	  syntax Int ::= clampHi(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
   103	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, _STEP:Int) => I
   104	       requires I  <Int LEN
   105	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then LEN -Int 1 #else LEN #fi
   106	       requires I >=Int LEN
   107	
   108	  // ==== build the strided sub-sequence (indices in range by construction) ====
   109	  syntax ValSeq ::= buildVS(ValSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   110	  rule buildVS(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   111	    => vCons(valSeqAt(VS, I), buildVS(VS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
   112	       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
   113	  rule buildVS(_:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .ValSeq
   114	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))
   115	
   116	  syntax IntSeq ::= buildIS(IntSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   117	  rule buildIS(IS:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   118	    => iCons(intSeqAt(IS, I), buildIS(IS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
   119	       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
   120	  rule buildIS(_:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .IntSeq
   121	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))

    Path("/candidate/verification.k"),

]

    r"^\s*(requires|module|imports|syntax|configuration|context|rule|claim|endmodule)\b"
)

records: list[dict[str, object]] = []

    lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    starts = [index for index, line in enumerate(lines) if start_re.match(line)]
    for position, start in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[position + 1] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        block_lines = lines[start:end]
        first = block_lines[0].strip()
        kind = start_re.match(block_lines[0]).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
        if kind not in {"syntax", "configuration", "context", "rule", "claim"}:
            continue

        attrs: list[str] = []
        if "[function" in block or re.search(r"\bfunction\b", block):
            attrs.append("function")
        for attr in (
            "total",
            "functional",
            "symbol",
            "no-evaluators",
            "macro",
            "macro-rec",
            "strict",
            "seqstrict",
            "owise",
            "concrete",
            "simplification",
        ):
            if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(attr)}\b", block):
                attrs.append(attr)
        priorities = re.findall(r"priority\(([^)]+)\)", block)
        if priorities:
            attrs.extend(f"priority({value})" for value in priorities)
        records.append(
            {
                "path": path,
                "line": start + 1,
                "end": end,
                "kind": kind,
                "attrs": attrs,
                "first": first,

            }

counts = Counter(str(record["kind"]) for record in records)

    "strict",

    print(

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Create a body-sensitive mutation that flips the program's equal-bit branch."""

from pathlib import Path


root = Path("/tmp/audit-work/11-string-xor")
source = root / "candidate" / "verification.k"
mutation_root = root / "body-mutation"

old = (
    'Assign(Name("result"), BinOp("+", Name("result"), Str("0"))),\n'
    '          Assign(Name("result"), BinOp("+", Name("result"), Str("1"))))'
)
new = (
    'Assign(Name("result"), BinOp("+", Name("result"), Str("1"))),\n'
    '          Assign(Name("result"), BinOp("+", Name("result"), Str("1"))))'
)
if text.count(old) != 1:
    raise RuntimeError(f"expected one body occurrence, found {text.count(old)}")
mutated_text = text.replace(old, new)
mutated.write_text(mutated_text, encoding="utf-8")
evidence_copy.write_text(mutated_text, encoding="utf-8")

term = (root / "regenerated-solution.mpy").read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip()
indented = "\n".join(f"      {line}" for line in term.splitlines())
pinning = f"""requires "verification.k"

module AUDIT-BODY-PINNING
  imports STRING-XOR-VERIFICATION

  claim
    <k>
      stringXorModule
      =>
{indented}
    </k>
endmodule
"""
(mutation_root / "audit-original-pinning-spec.k").write_text(pinning, encoding="utf-8")
print(f"source={source}")
print(f"mutated={mutated}")
print(f"evidence_copy={evidence_copy}")
print("mutation=equal branch appends '1' instead of '0'")
print("BODY_MUTATION_GENERATED")

# Static rule review

This review is keyed to every record in `rule_inventory.md`; the one-row-per-ID
decision ledger is `rule_decisions.tsv`.

## Scope and result

The inventory contains 959 records: 237 syntax declarations, one configuration,
five contexts, 714 rules, and two claims. It contains 115 `[total]`
declarations, 25 `symbol`/`no-evaluators` boundaries, 48 concrete rules, 33
priority occurrences, and no simplification or functional declarations. Every
record has an explicit decision in the TSV. No candidate proof-local rule is an
operational bridge, simplification, priority rewrite, opaque oracle, or
unconstrained result producer.

## Constructor-to-rule map for `solution.mpy`

| Submitted construct | Declaration/evaluation path | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `Module`, statement list | `syntax.k`; `core.k` `#loadAll` and statement sequencing | Exact left-to-right module execution. |
| `ImportFrom("typing","List")` | `syntax.k`; `controls.k` non-math import rule | It is executed as typing-only no-op. Python would bind `List`, but the name is never read and this cannot affect the function return. |
| `FuncDef`, closure, call, return | `functions.k` and `call.k`; `core.k` lookup | Exact name binding, two-argument binding, call frame, body, return, frame restoration/deallocation. No closure escapes. |
| docstring `Expr(Str(...))` | `str.k` literal; `controls.k` expression discard | Exact inert docstring behavior for this theorem. |
| name assignments | strict syntax; `controls.k` assignment | RHS evaluates first and current function scope is updated. |
| `zip(a,b)` | lookup/call; `builtins.k` lines 164 and 171-174 | Exact string-code pairing and truncation at the shorter input. |
| `For` | strict iterable; `controls.k` lines 69-74 | Iterable evaluated once; each yielded pair is bound, body runs, and loop recurs. |
| tuple target `(x,y)` | `tuple.k` `#bindTgt/#unpackSeq` | Binds `x` then `y` from the exact two-element tuple. |
| `Compare(x == y)` | `operators.k`; `str.k` line 25 | Both operands evaluate left-to-right and code-sequence equality selects the branch. |
| string `+` | `operators.k`; `str.k` `seqConcat` and line 24 | Exact immutable string-code concatenation. |
| `If` | strict test; `controls.k` branch rules | Exactly one branch executes from truthiness of the Bool comparison. |

Every material operation and control effect therefore executes under the fixed
semantics. The program path allocates no heap objects and raises no modeled
exception; heap, heap counter, return state, stack, exit code, and non-local
scopes are correctly framed.

## Module decisions, exhaustive ranges

- `INV-0001`–`INV-0928` are the supplied fixed semantics. The detailed ledger
  records every item. The used path above was checked rule-by-rule for
  evaluation order, guards, priority, state footprint, and control. Remaining
  modules are operation-specific and unreachable from this submitted
  constructor tree.
- `INV-0001`–`INV-0017` (assert/bool): coherent success/failure and
  short-circuit rules; only concrete smoke assertions use `assert`.
- `INV-0018`–`INV-0192` (builtins): zip's creation/yield/done guards are
  disjoint and complete for string pairs. Other builtins are unused.
- `INV-0193`–`INV-0216` (call): callee and arguments evaluate in order; the
  closure dispatch preserves the caller continuation and all state cells.
- `INV-0217`–`INV-0247` (comprehension/concrete): unused. The LLVM-only rules
  are not imported by the proof definition.
- `INV-0248`–`INV-0284` (controls): the used assignment, import, expression,
  if, and for rules are exact; priority rules only dereference heap refs, which
  this path never has. Break/continue/while are unused.
- `INV-0285`–`INV-0368` (core): configuration, lookup, sequencing, builtins
  scope, literal evaluation, truthiness, and structural folds are coherent.
  Priority-40 cell lookup cannot match the plain function frame (no `$cells`).
- `INV-0369`–`INV-0563` (dict/float): unused limited sublanguages. All opaque
  float symbols are fixed-semantics trust boundaries with no target dependent.
- `INV-0564`–`INV-0599` (functions/int): the unannotated-closure path is exact.
  Cell closures and Python integer operators are otherwise unused.
- `INV-0600`–`INV-0797` (iterator/list/methods/operators/range/set/sort):
  iterator declarations and generic operator dispatch support the used
  zip/string path; collection methods, range, set, and opaque sorts are unused.
- `INV-0798`–`INV-0928` (str/subscript/syntax/tuple): string literal,
  concatenate, compare, grammar, and tuple unpacking match the program.
  Index/slice rules are unused.

The fresh LLVM build reported incomplete match coverage for `mapStrVS`,
`floorFI`, `toF`, `ceilF`, `joinCodes`, and `valSeqAt`. Their precise inventory
records are marked `LIMITATION_UNUSED_NO_FALSE_TARGET_CONCLUSION`; none of
their symbols or callers occurs in the submitted term, proof-local helpers, or
claims. These are fixed-semantics coverage limitations, not equations enabling
a false XOR conclusion. No claim of global Python completeness is made.

The named opaque boundaries `md5hexCodes`, float operations/conversions,
`sortVS`, and `sortKeyVS` are likewise all unused. There is no empirical or
opaque bridge on the material target path.

## Candidate proof-local decisions

- `INV-0929`–`INV-0930`: `binaryCode` is exactly membership in ASCII
  `{48,49}` and is total.
- `INV-0931`–`INV-0933`: the two `xorCode` guards are disjoint; under
  `binaryCode(A) ∧ binaryCode(B)` they cover equality and inequality and return
  the four-row XOR truth table.
- `INV-0934`–`INV-0940`: `xorAcc` and `binaryCodes` recurse structurally.
  The two base cases are disjoint and implement zip truncation; the recursive
  case appends exactly one XOR code.
- `INV-0941`–`INV-0947`: `xorLastX/Y` recurse over the same paired suffix and
  exactly model the last tuple binding, retaining the prior value when no pair
  exists.
- `INV-0948`–`INV-0957`: target, loop body, function body, closure, and module
  are definitional aliases only. The constructor-pinning claim proves the
  module alias equals the trusted-regenerated term. The body mutation changes
  this term and makes the real proof stick.
- `INV-0958`: the loop claim is a fixed-semantics auxiliary execution theorem,
  universally quantified over `CONT`. Its match context and justification
  context coincide: the exact target/body, current environment/frame, binary
  remaining suffixes, arbitrary continuation, and framed untouched cells.
  It returns normally and cannot discard or fabricate control.
- `INV-0959`: the entry claim starts from a realizable initial configuration,
  loads the pinned module, calls the selected `"string_xor"` binding, and
  requires the returned `Str` to equal `xorAcc(.IntSeq,A,B)`. The result is not
  fresh, existential, tautological, or merely implied one way.

No guards overlap with disagreeing right-hand sides, every recursive helper
descends on an algebraic sequence, and all `[total]` proof-local declarations
cover their stated constructor domains. No false-conclusion witness exists for
any candidate proof-local rule; accordingly none is labeled unsound.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Bounded structural inspection of the untrusted generation trace."""
+
+from collections import Counter
+import glob
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+paths = [Path(path) for path in glob.glob("/generation-evidence/codex-trace/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True)]
+print(f"trace_files={len(paths)}")
+for path in sorted(paths):
+    data = path.read_bytes()
+    top_types: Counter[str] = Counter()
+    payload_types: Counter[str] = Counter()
+    tool_names: Counter[str] = Counter()
+    command_summaries: list[str] = []
+    agent_messages: list[str] = []
+    line_count = 0
+    for line_count, line in enumerate(data.decode("utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
+        record = json.loads(line)
+        top_types[str(record.get("type"))] += 1
+        payload = record.get("payload", {})
+        payload_type = str(payload.get("type"))
+        payload_types[payload_type] += 1
+        if payload_type in {"custom_tool_call", "function_call"}:
+            name = str(payload.get("name"))
+            tool_names[name] += 1
+            text = str(payload.get("input") or payload.get("arguments") or "")
+            first_nonempty = next(
+                (part.strip() for part in text.splitlines() if part.strip()), ""
+            )
+            command_summaries.append(
+                f"line={line_count} tool={name} first_line={first_nonempty[:240]}"
+            )
+        if payload_type == "message" and payload.get("role") == "assistant":
+            texts = [
+                item.get("text", "")
+                for item in payload.get("content", [])
+                if isinstance(item, dict)
+            ]
+            if texts:
+                agent_messages.append(" ".join(texts))
+    print(f"path={path}")
+    print(f"sha256={hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()}")
+    print(f"lines={line_count}")
+    print(f"top_types={dict(top_types)}")
+    print(f"payload_types={dict(payload_types)}")

+# Independent adversarial review: 11-string-xor
+
+The candidate contains a legitimate partial-correctness proof of the submitted
+program for the full source-contract domain. I reconstructed the definitions
+from source, reran the target claims, mechanically pinned the theorem term to
+the trusted translator output, exhaustively inventoried the K theory, changed
+the executed body, and rejected a fresh false postcondition.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+
+`/audit-input.json` declares `record_layout = legacy-selected-stage1` and
+`semantics_mode = SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`. This is coherent with the mounts:
+`/reference/reference-semantics` is present and is a non-symlink directory.

+
+All records required for `legacy-selected-stage1` are present, readable,

+The candidate mount contains no symlink or special-file entries. The candidate
+`prompt.py` and `py2mpy.py` are byte-identical to their trusted mounts.
+Recursively comparing the submitted and trusted supplied-semantics trees gives
+the same 25 relative entries, types, and file bytes, with no missing,
+additional, renamed, or changed entry. An independent canonical JSON tree
+manifest also gives the same digest for both semantics trees. The launcher's

+independent manifest digest rather than equating unlike hash namespaces.
+
+Evidence:
+[integrity script](/audit-output/evidence/stage1_integrity.py),
+[integrity log](/audit-output/evidence/stage1_integrity.log), and
+[bounded trace summary](/audit-output/evidence/generation_trace_summary.log).
+There is no infrastructure breach.
+
+## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks
+
+The trusted prompt requires `string_xor(a: str, b: str) -> str`: both inputs
+contain only `0` and `1`, and the result is the pointwise binary XOR string.
+The trusted canonical implementation applies a four-case equality/XOR helper
+over Python `zip(a,b)`, so unequal inputs truncate to the shorter length. Empty
+binary strings are therefore supported.
+
+The candidate implements the same algorithm iteratively: it initializes an
+empty result, iterates through `zip(a,b)`, appends `"0"` when the characters
+are equal and `"1"` otherwise, and returns the accumulator. It neither fixes
+the length nor strengthens the input contract.
+
+Running the trusted `/reference/py2mpy.py` over the scratch copy of
+`solution.py` produced SHA-256
+`6dc4a5199d3c6f87b07ef8a7a901fad25e3105d323aa76e079880a67ce6be154`,
+byte-identical to submitted `solution.mpy`.
+
+The independent differential test imports both the trusted canonical entry
+point and candidate entry point and also uses a separately written four-row
+XOR table. It checks the documented example, both/one-sided empty cases, all
+four branch pairs, both unequal-length directions, every pair of binary
+strings whose individual length is at most six (16,129 pairs), and 2,000
+deterministically generated pairs up to length 256. All 18,141 cases agree;
+there are zero mismatches.
+
+Evidence:
+[differential script](/audit-output/evidence/differential_test.py) and
+[translation/differential log](/audit-output/evidence/stage2_fidelity.log).
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+I copied source artifacts to `/tmp/audit-work/11-string-xor` and used new
+output-definition names after confirming they did not exist. No
+candidate-provided K definition or cache was reused. K reports version
+7.1.293, matching the campaign record.

+1. LLVM compilation of supplied `semantics.k` with main module `MPY-KRUN` and
+   syntax module `MPY-SYNTAX`: exit 0.

+   `NoExc`, and exit code 0.

+   `STRING-XOR-VERIFICATION`: exit 0.
+4. `loop-invariant` selected alone: `#Top`, exit 0.

+   `solution-correct`: `#Top`, exit 0.
+
+The end-to-end claim intentionally uses the loop claim as its circularity, so
+the valid target command includes both. A diagnostic that filtered the helper
+claim out was interrupted and is not counted as a positive target run; it is
+preserved in `stage3_reconstruction.log`. The clean completed run separately
+proves the auxiliary and then proves the complete selected target set.
+
+The compiler's LLVM warnings concern incomplete totalizations of operations
+not reached by this program (`mapStrVS`, several float helpers, `joinCodes`,
+and `valSeqAt`). They are addressed in Stage 5 and do not replace or weaken
+the successful target runs.
+
+Evidence:
+[reconstruction script](/audit-output/evidence/stage3_reconstruction.sh) and
+[completed reconstruction log](/audit-output/evidence/stage3_reconstruction_complete.log).
+
+## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning
+
+### Entry-claim meanings
+
+`loop-invariant` starts at the actual internal `#loop` for a string
+`zipObjS(A,B)`, with the exact translated tuple target and exact translated
+conditional body followed by an arbitrary continuation `CONT`. The current
+scope contains original arguments, current result prefix, and current `x/y`.
+The remaining code sequences are binary. It proves that the loop consumes the
+shorter remaining suffix, appends the corresponding XOR codes, leaves `x/y`
+at their last paired one-character strings (or their prior values when no pair
+exists), preserves the arguments/parent/other scopes, and continues with
+`CONT`.
+
+`solution-correct` starts from a realizable initial configuration with empty
+module scope, supplied builtins, empty heap/stack, and no return or exception.
+For arbitrary finite binary code sequences `A` and `B`, it loads the submitted
+module and calls the selected `"string_xor"` binding. It requires the returned
+value to be exactly `str(xorAcc(.IntSeq,A,B))` and fixes the final module scope.
+The return is not a fresh variable, existential, tautology, or one-way
+implication.
+
+### Mechanical program identity
+
+The audit generated a reachability claim whose destination constructor term
+was read directly from the trusted-regenerated `solution.mpy`. Under the fresh
+candidate definition, `stringXorModule` equals that exact term and the claim
+prints `#Top`. This includes the typing import, function binding, parameters,
+docstring, assignments, `zip` loop, both branches, and return.
+
+A separate body-sensitivity mutation changed the executed equal-bit branch
+from appending `"0"` to appending `"1"` inside `stringXorLoopBody`. Because
+`stringXorBody` and `stringXorModule` expand through that alias, this changes
+the program term actually executed by the entry claim. The original
+constructor-pinning claim then fails with `WarnStuckClaimState`, visibly
+showing the mutated `"1"` constructor; the positive proof also fails on the
+expected disagreement between output prefixes. Thus the proof is sensitive
+to the real body, not merely an external source file.
+
+### Satisfiable witnesses and concrete substitution
+
+For `A = "010"` and `B = "110"` (code sequences
+`48,49,48` and `49,49,48`), both binary predicates reduce to true.
